In summary, our research is concerned with

identifying the molecular basis of probiotic activity in Lactobacilli, in particular L. salivarius sub-sp. salivarius, a probiotic strain which was originally isolated from intestinal mucosal tissues and which has subsequently been shown in a pilot trial to alleviate symptoms associated mild-moderate ulcerative colitis.
the development of probiotic bacteria that can adhere to the intestinal mucosa and provide a protective effect against the onset of inflammatory bowel disease.
the development of novel probiotic strains that are able to colonise the gut, and to modulate host immunity, thereby improving the health and well being of the host.

the cell wall proteome of Lactobacilli salivarius sub sp. salivarius is highly dynamic and is subject to significant change in response to environmental cues.

the cell wall-associated proteomic profile of L. salivarius sub. salivarius strain UCC118 correlates with the growth phase of the bacterium, and that the cell wall is an important factor in the adherence ability and potential virulence of the bacterium.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Lactobacilli are not simply probiotic organisms but rather are a complex community of organisms with a range of attributes, some of which may be similar to those of pathogenic bacteria, but which are attenuated in their expression.
Lactobacilli may be able to adhere to intestinal tissue and modulate the inflammatory response by mimicking virulence factors associated with Listeria monocogenes.
the cell wall proteome of Lactobacilli salivarius Ucc118 has a significant impact on its ability to adhere to host tissue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
L. salivarius is capable of expressing proteins that are associated with virulence and pathogenicity.

Lactobacilli can mimic pathogenic bacteria, and that the ability to do so is linked to growth phase and may be due to the presence of cell wall-associated proteins that are also found in pathogenic bacteria.
the Lactobacilli proteome is highly conserved, and that the cell wall-associated proteins of probiotic bacteria may play an important role in the beneficial attributes of these organisms.
